en.headline: Hung Shing Temple and Stanley Mosque declared monuments
en.dek: The Development Bureau gazetted the Wan Chai temple and the mosque inside Stanley Prison as statutory monuments on Friday.
body: The government gazetted two historic buildings as statutory monuments on Friday. The Antiquities Authority, who is the Secretary for Development, made the declarations under the Antiquities and Monuments Ordinance.

Hung Shing Temple on Queen's Road East in Wan Chai is one of the oldest surviving temples in the district. The government said it is thought to have been built between 1847 and 1852 and is dedicated to Hung Shing, described as the god of the southern sea. It said the temple was an important place of worship and, in its early years, a place where worshippers installed ancestral tablets.

The government said the building keeps much of its original form, including stone carvings, plaster mouldings, granite figures and a Shiwan roof ridge added in 1909, and sits against a natural rock face in a Lingnan folk style.

Stanley Mosque, inside Stanley Prison, was built between 1936 and 1937. The government said it is the second-oldest mosque in Hong Kong and the only one inside a prison complex. It was proposed, funded and built by Muslim staff of Indian and Pakistani origin in the then Prisons Department, together with the local Indian community, and was modelled on the Badshahi Mosque in Lahore, with a symmetrical plan oriented towards the Kaaba in Mecca.

zh.headline: 灣仔洪聖古廟及赤柱清真寺列法定古蹟
zh.dek: 發展局周五刊憲，古物事務監督根據《古物及古蹟條例》宣布兩座建築列為法定古蹟。
body: 政府周五刊憲，把兩座歷史建築列為法定古蹟。古物事務監督，即發展局局長，根據《古物及古蹟條例》作出宣布。
灣仔皇后大道東的洪聖古廟是區內現存最古老廟宇之一。政府表示，古廟估計建於1847至1852年間，供奉被稱為「南海之神」的洪聖，長期是區內祭祀場所，早期亦有善信在廟內安放神主牌。
政府說，古廟原貌保持度高，石雕、灰塑、花崗石人物雕像，以及1909年加建的石灣脊飾仍然完好，並以嶺南民間建築手法與毗鄰天然岩石相融。
赤柱清真寺位於赤柱監獄內，建於1936至1937年間。政府表示，這是本港第二古老的清真寺，亦是唯一一座坐落於監獄建築群的清真寺，由當時監獄署的印度及巴基斯坦籍穆斯林員工聯同本地印度社群倡議、捐助及興建，以巴基斯坦拉合爾巴德夏希清真寺為藍本，布局對稱，朝向麥加克爾白。
